items.author: Priya Menon
items.topicSummary: GenAI pilots were killed because no one owned the surrounding process, not because the model failed.
items.comment:
This is the conversation more delivery teams need to have.

A pilot that never inherits exception-handling, handoffs, and ownership is still a demo — production starts when the process is redesigned around the agent, not when the accuracy slide looks good.
items.whySelected: Direct hit on pilot-to-production and process ownership.

items.author: Daniel Okonkwo
items.topicSummary: Multi-agent value is blocked by operating-model gaps, not missing frameworks.
items.comment:
Appreciate you framing this as an operating model, not a stack diagram.

Until start rights, review rights, disagreement SLAs, and audit sit on one page, extra agents mostly manufacture coordination cost.
items.whySelected: Opens a real thread on AI operating models.

items.author: Ananya Rao
items.topicSummary: Agile AI delivery works when evals and human review are treated as backlog, not afterthought.
items.comment:
Thank you for naming the sprint-review failure mode so plainly.

Putting evaluation sets and human-in-the-loop checks into acceptance criteria is how AI work stops being theatre and starts surviving contact with production.
items.whySelected: Concrete Agile practice for AI projects, not a slogan.

items.author: Marcus Hill
items.topicSummary: Agent adoption depends on mapping copy-steps and deciding which exceptions the agent may close.
items.comment:
Glad you called the unglamorous part the actual job.

The map of copy-steps and exception rights is the design artefact; without it, integration work just wraps a model around a process that cannot absorb an agent.
items.whySelected: Process redesign for agents, stated as an operating practice.

items.author: Sofia Alvarez
items.topicSummary: Working AI governance is inventory, kill switch, scheduled evals, and named owners.
items.comment:
Production hygiene is the right name for this.

A policy PDF does not run an estate — inventory, classification, a kill switch, evals on a clock, and a named owner for each agent does.
items.whySelected: Governance as operations, which is where comments stay useful.
